To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the percentage of estradiol receptor positive tumors in relation to clinical staging, menopausal state, histology, free survival time and survival time is higher than that of receptor negative tumors.

in the mammary carcinoma patients the percentage of receptor-positive tumors is highest in the pre- and peri-menopausal women, lowest in those who have been in menopause for more than 5 years and highest in the patients with small, well differentiated tumors, lowest in the patients with large, poorly differentiated tumors.

in 50% of all mammary tumors, estrogen receptors are detectable, and that in 50-70% of these cases, a favourable clinical course can be expected, whereas the receptor negative tumors show a more unfavourable prognosis.

the percentage of positive receptor cases in mammary carcinomas is in the range of 40% in all stages and in all histologic tumor types, but the highest percentages of receptor positive cases are found in tumors of pre- and perimenopausal women, in tumors of low histologic grade and low clinical stages, in tumors with long free intervals and in tumors with long survival times.
